text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
*Hard-right National Alliance party said it would present a motion of no-confidence in Agriculture minister Michele Pinto over his handling of a row with dairy farmers over EU milk quotas (all).

* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema seems set to take the chairmanship of a new bi-cameral commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms, as most opposition parties gave their approval (all).
* Prosecutors asked an Italian court to jail Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti for one year and eight months on accounting fraud charges (all).

* Guido Rossi, former head of the Italian bourse regulator Consob, will reportedly be named as head of state telecoms holding STET. The post of managing director, currently held by Ernesto Pascale, will be given to Tommaso Tommasi di Vignano, currently director-general of Telecom Italia (La Repubblica).

* Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said STET must pay the state 120 billion lire as part of a complex balancing act involving Italy's two mobile phone operators. As a result, Italy's second mobile phone company, Omnitel, will not receive 60 billion lire in reimbursementes from STET's operating units (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi will meet today with metalworkers trade unions to try and reach a solution over a long-running pay dispute (all).

* Italy's public sector borrowing requirement in January should be better than expected, with unnamed sources predicting a break-even or, at worse, a 2-3 trillion lire deficit. Forecasts were for a 5 trillion lire deficit (Sole 24 Ore).
* Florence's soccer team Fiorentina, owned by media mogul Vittorio Cecchi Gori, plans stock market listing (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
